Header: Phytophthora infestans Amharic: Yedinich wag; Oromiffa: Xoolaksaa mosee

Prevention: Prevention
Use disease free planting material.
Inspect seed potatoes to make sure there is no disease before planting
Use quality declared seed (QDS).
IDM improved potato varieties:
Gudene, Belete, Jalene, Zenegena, Chiro, Bubu, Gorobella
Crop rotation - avoid planting tomato, pepper and other solanaceous crops if late blight is present.
Remove left overs plants that can serve as source of the inoculum
Plant early.
For ware potatoes adopt 0.75m
X 0.30m between rows and plants and 0.30m
X 0.60m for seed use.
Use the recommended fertilizer rate since the pathogen develops fast under high nitrogen conditions
Do not over water and maintain good drainage
Hill or earth up the soil over the planted seed potatoes can protect the tubers from the disease
Dehulm and remove the vines 15 days before harvest.
Do not compost cull piles, chop and bury
During harvest remove damaged and diseased tubers.
Avoid wounding tubers and remove soil before transport
Remove infected seed tubers from the store and bury
Monitoring: Inspect the field for disease every other day after plant emergence
Leaf lesions are highly variable depending on environmental condition and cultivar
Initial symptoms: small, pale or dark green spots with yellow halos.
Growing rapidly into large brown to purple/black lesions that eventually kill the plant.
Under moist conditions, white cottony structures appears at the edge of the lesion mostly on the underside of the leaves
Infected stem have irregular lesions surrowned by white cottony structure and are brittle
Symptom on infected tubers: irregular, slightly depressed areas brown to purple in colour.
On the skin they can show as redish brown superficial or deep rotted areas accompanied by secondory infection
Scout suspect low-lying areas which tend to dry out more slowly, the disease might be more likely to occur here
When symptoms are at around 5% serverity carry out control methods
Direct Control: Remove the diseased plants and plant parts by bagging them to avoid producing large numbers of spores that could put other plants and nearby farmers at risk
Destroy diseased plant parts outside the field by burying 1m under the ground
Kill vines totally prior to harvest because late blight does not sporulate on dead plant tissue.
Infected tubers should not be stored.
Monitor storage carefully for any sign of tuber decay
Mancozeb (Ridom 80% WP, Sabozeb 80% WP, Ethiozeb 80% WP)
Apply at a rate of 1.5-2.5 kg/ha.
Apply at a rate of 2-3 kg/ ha.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
All products toxic to fish and aquatic organisms, do not spray near water.
